# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-core-comm-combined

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Tests **all three communication interventions combined** (Message Delivery Timing + Message Board / Threading + Message Intent Tags) on the 10-pair `core` subset with `vertex_ai/gemini-3-8-flash` (`high` thinking, 100 steps, compaction at 28K, per-turn step counter, `$40` cost cap). Evaluates how full structured threading, speech-act intents, and turn-boundary buffering interact on a stronger reasoning model compared against `coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-core-stepcounter` (4/10).

## Observations

- Passed **5/10 (50%, all 5 clean or identical merges)** — +10 percentage points above the 4/10 `coop --git` baseline and matching 5/10 `solo`, while cutting merge conflicts in half (from 2 to 1: same-function pair `react_hook_form_task/153` merged cleanly; only `dspy_task/8563` conflicted).
- Reduced total message volume by **35%** relative to the baseline (from 228 messages to 148, or 14.8 per pair) and lowered cost (`$11.89` vs. `$13.16`), with 100% thread resolution (13/13 threads resolved; `FYI`: 26, `Request`: 24, `ACK`: 20, `Response`: 10, only 2 flag-syntax rejections).
- Scored 1 pair below `intents` alone (5/10 vs. 6/10 because `llama_index_task/17244` merged cleanly with only Feature A passing), reinforcing that `intents` carries the primary coordination gain on `gemini-3.8-flash` while `threading` adds minor protocol overhead.
